citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee did not communicate an issue observed during daily observations to the attending veterinarian in a timely
manner. At the time of inspection, a male Havanese puppy (# 523262) born May 23, 2026 was missing the left rear leg,
removed at the level of the hip. The area over the hip was already healed and per the licensee injury to the leg occurred
from the mother overgrooming soon after birth. The veterinarian was only made aware of this when he stopped by to drop
off supplies a few weeks ago. Although per the veterinarian, “nothing could be done to treat”, the licensee should have
communicated this medical finding to the veterinarian in a timely matter to ensure the AV has knowledge of incidents of
this nature and given the opportunity to provide adequate guidance and care plans for health-related issues and injuries.
All future incidents of this nature or any other health care noted through daily observations must be conveyed to the
veterinarian in a timely manner so that he may make determination for care.
Correct by: June 12, 2026

Multiple dogs did not receive a head-to-tail physical exam within a 12-month period. Sixteen (16) dogs had an exam dated
09/24/24 and then another exam was completed 01/03/26. Twenty-eight (28) dogs had exams on 10/8/24 and then again
on 12/02/2025. Per this regulation, all dogs must have a completed head to tail physical examination completed not once
less than every 12- months to ensure any potential health issues can be noted and a treatment and care plan created for
the overall health and well being of the dogs. The licensee needs to work with her veterinarian to ensure there is
adequate time to plan for these annual exams so they do not get pushed out further than the required 12 month period.
Correct by: July 26, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
